name: When should I consider repairing existing drywall versus complete replacement?

mainEntity.name: When should I consider repairing existing drywall versus complete replacement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing existing drywall is often suitable for small holes, cracks, or minor water damage. If the damage is localized and structurally sound, patching can be a cost-effective solution. However, complete replacement is recommended for extensive water damage causing structural compromise, widespread mold growth, or large sections of severely damaged or crumbling drywall. A practical tradeoff is evaluating the extent of the damage: repairing multiple large sections can sometimes be more time-consuming and less durable than a full replacement, especially if underlying issues like framing damage are present. Our team can assess the damage and recommend the most practical approach.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repairing drywall is best for minor damage, while replacement is needed for extensive issues like structural water damage or widespread mold.
